summary: README is a short reviewer handoff: the heap-looks-complete trap, the WAL/visibility/CDC/apply/recover invariants, and catalogctl scenario families that distinguish plausible wrong behavior. No task.toml explanation fields; that is not a defect. Voice is terse and unpadded. Harbor run commands are present. It is not a file-by-file oracle walkthrough.

evidence.observation: Three unlabeled families are present. Difficulty: snapshot isolation, constraints, indexes, logical CDC, and replica apply must agree on one WAL; a complete-looking heap can still leak an uncommitted crash insert into CDC, rewind a replica slot, or leave indexes on aborted versions. Solution: keep the Go catalog/WAL protocol; xmin/xmax visibility; constraints see writer snapshot plus write set; indexes rebuild from committed-visible rows after COMMIT and recover; decode walks committed WAL; apply is LSN-monotonic, epoch-fenced, and FK-ordered inside a txn; checkpoint redo skips uncommitted records; inspect does not recover; warehouse stays put. Verification: isolated copies of transferred /app/catalog; catalogctl usage errors leave WAL untouched; frozen-tenant and hold-qty rejects; unique/FK; decode skips abort; apply rejects stale epoch without advancing confirmed_lsn; recover drops the crash insert; indexes match visible heap; health schema and warehouse bytes. Harbor stb harbor run oracle/nop commands and solution/solve.sh as reference entrypoint. No patch-file sequence, no helper names, no hidden fixture paths.
No difficulty_explanation, solution_explanation, or verification_explanation fields. Packet states that is expected when README covers those families.

README does not copy the agent ticket. Instruction is the bounce incident plus public catalogctl/contract rules. README restates coupling and invariants for a human reviewer and adds Harbor how-to-run. Overlap is domain fact, not an instruction dump.

High-level suite matches README claims: drives catalogctl on isolated tree copies; unknown flag/command and missing --input leave WAL; inspect/empty-check do not recover; frozen tenant, hold-qty, unique, and FK rejects; decode skips uncommitted crash sku; apply monotonic/stale-epoch/FK order; recover drops uncommitted insert and rebuilds indexes; health schema; warehouse bytes unchanged. README names those distinguishing outcomes, not pytest internals or fixture files.
Canonical golang:1.24-bookworm digest; builds cmd/seed and runs it at image build. Supports the seeded-inventory claim. No non-canonical-base justification is required.

Difficulty is the missed state interaction, not generic multi-component filler. Solution is invariant-focused, not a diff. Verification names scenario purpose without comprehensive/robust claims. No stock documentation phrases from the anti-pattern bank.

Aligns with human difficulty/solution/verification pairs: plausible partial heap-visibility fix still fails CDC/replica/index agreement; authoritative WAL/visibility invariants; live catalogctl families that rule out those wrong classes.

Section 12 requires human README covering difficulty, solution, and verification; not shown to agents. README supplies those, does not copy instruction.md, and does not dump oracle internals beyond naming solution/solve.sh as the Harbor reference entrypoint.
